raw.translational: Understanding the shared role of SLC16A1 in these two distinct metabolic disorders could inform therapeutic strategies. For exercise-induced hyperinsulinism, interventions aimed at normalizing glucose-insulin homeostasis in the context of impaired lactate transport might be beneficial. For ketoacidosis, strategies to mitigate the accumulation of ketone bodies and lactate, or to bypass the impaired transporter, could be explored.

partners.mechanism_chain: SLC16A1 (HGNC:11074) —DECREASES→ lactate (CHEBI:15361); lactate (CHEBI:15361) —DISRUPTS→ glucose metabolism and insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-69621); glucose metabolism and insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-69621) —LEADS_TO→ exercise-induced hyperinsulinism (MONDO:0012396); UGT1A1 (HGNC:12217) —DISRUPTS→ bilirubin (CHEBI:16440); bilirubin (CHEBI:16440) —DISRUPTS→ bilirubin metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-194247); bilirubin metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-194247) —LEADS_TO→ neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (MONDO:0009383). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 impair lactate transport, disrupting glucose metabolism and insulin secretion, leading to exercise-induced hyperinsulinism. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in UGT1A1 impair the conjugation of bilirubin, disrupting bilirubin metabolism and causing neonatal hyperbilirubinemia. While the primary causal genes and immediate pathways differ, both conditions represent disruptions in critical metabolic pathways impacting cellular homeostasis and organismal function.
